sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Sega and Creative Assembly remove Total War: Shogun 2 remaster from sale as it "falls short of both your expectations and our own standards"
sources.text: Recently launched title has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam, with players citing AI upscaling and performance issues Sega and Creative Assembly have temporarily withdrawn Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition from sale in response to concerns about AI upscaling and other performance issues. Since its October 13 launch, the remaster has received overwhelmingly negative reviews on Steam. Players have reported that assets such as unit cards and new cutscenes display AI-generated features , including extra fingers and armor merging into characters' bodies. As described on Steam , the "underlying graphics technology has been brought to modern standards to take advantage of new methods in rendering," resulting in improved graphics and textures. In response, both companies issued a joint statement acknowledging that the game "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards." "We've seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be." "As a result we are working with platform holders to temporarily remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues. Existing owners will still be able to access and play the game." "We are working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 – Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War." Earlier this year, Sega faced criticism for its use of generative AI in Crazy Taxi: World Tour. The game's Steam page included a generative AI disclaimer, which clarified that Sega uses the technology "as a support tool for developers, aiming to provide better content to our users and enable developers to focus more on creative tasks." "We have used such generative AI support tools during development of Crazy Taxi: World Tour. No AI was used in reference to the performers in game." In a statement to Game Informer , Sega clarified that generative AI was "used to support our teams during the development of background assets" and that "assets generated were still subject to review by the development team."

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: The Shogun 2 remaster is so bad, Sega is removing it from sale and bringing back the original
sources.text: Sega admits Shogun 2 - Complete Edition "has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards," so it's going back to the drawing board. Just two days after the disastrous release of Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition, Sega says it is removing the game from sale and putting the original back until it gets things sorted out. Which brings us to now: After two days of silence, Sega has finally made a move: It says "the current experience is not where it needs to be," and is thus "working with platform holders to remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues." Anyone who purchased Shogun 2 - Complete Edition will still have access to it, but how (or if) Sega will enable them to go back to playing the original version wasn't clarified. Pulling Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from sale and restoring the original is obviously the right move, and today's message promises improvements to the game to bring it more in-line with expectations, so hopefully we'll see some of the more glaring bugs and QoL issues resolved. But all of this is still a very bad look for Creative Assembly, which has had something of an up-and-down history with its games and players over the years. It's a particular shame coming so soon after the company's successful launch of the Lords of the End Times expansion for Total War: Warhammer, which has been widely praised. The announcement of Total War: Warhammer 40k also has a lot of RTS fans, and WH40K sickos, very excited, and nonsense like this really takes the wind out of those sails: If Shogun 2 - Complete Edition allowed out the door in this condition, how are fans supposed to expect better in the future? A few fans have also pointed out that in 2024, Sega's Aegis-CWA union accused the company of outsourcing Q&A and some localization services, resulting in the layoffs of 61 people. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. As I write this, Shogun 2 - Complete Edition remains available for purchase on Steam , GOG , and the Epic Games Store —Sega has not specified when it will be removed. It has also not yet responded to the accusations of gen AI usage in Shogun 2 - Complete Edition—I've reached out to ask about that and will update if I receive a reply. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill. sources.text: Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition is being removed after users discovered bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition is being removed after users discovered bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. Sega is removing Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from storefronts following a disastrous launch where users complained about issues like bugs and upscaling that appears to have been done by AI. Complete Edition , a remaster of the 2011 strategy game, launched on Tuesday, and it bundled the main game and all of its DLC with promised upgrades including “improved visuals,” “1440p and 4K UI scaling,” and modernized controls. It has an “Overwhelmingly Negative” rating on Steam , where it has already been pulled, and posts on Reddit showcase artwork that users believe AI messed up. “We’re aware that Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” Sega and developer Creative Assembly wrote in a post . “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be.” The two companies say they will “reinstate the original game,” and existing owners will “still be able to access ” Complete Edition . Sega and Creative Assembly say that they are “working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 - Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War.” A studio called Mataboo is also listed as a developer for the game on Steam, and Mataboo highlights its work on the game on its website .

sources.title: Modern Warfare 4 Emerges to Best Call of Duty Steam Rating in a Decade
sources.text: Modern Warfare 4’s campaign early access portion went live yesterday , and fans everywhere have poured in to get a glimpse of this year’s hotly anticipated Call of Duty title. The marketing loop has built up immeasurable hype for this year’s instalment of the first-person shooter series, and folks are eagerly awaiting the arrival of multiplayer, DMZ , and the esports action to commence. On Steam , Modern Warfare 4’s earliest impressions have pushed the franchise into a realm it hasn’t seen for many years . It’s very early days, but the review sentiment has, at the time of writing, made Modern Warfare 4 the top-rated Call of Duty game, on Steam , in over a decade. We have limited numbers to play with, but as I publish this article, Modern Warfare 4 has managed to rack up a positive review rating of 81.15% on Steam. That makes it the best-rated Call of Duty game since 2015’s Black Ops III. Here’s the spread of ratings for the last eleven Call of Duty games on Steam (note: MW4’s rating, especially, will change drastically in the coming days and weeks): What’s more interesting in that list is that Black Ops Cold War, the ‘rushed’ title that everyone seemed to hate, ranks higher than Modern Warfare 2019, the ‘turning point’ game that refreshed the franchise, introduced Warzone, and rebooted the MW sub-series. I will stress again that the review score will have likely changed by the time you see this article, but it’s indicative of the bigger picture; that’s for sure. And I’ll also stress that the review scores are coming from the earliest adopters, those who wanted to pay extra or early to get the first look at the game’s campaign, a week ahead of the global launch. They’re the players who are more primed to enjoy Modern Warfare 4. You’ve also got a tiny pool to work with, with the game having secured only 900 user reviews at the time of writing. The expectations were high, the technological leaps look to have pushed Modern Warfare 4 to dizzying new heights, and folks seem to be loving it. At least, they’re loving the campaign . The multiplayer portion of the game is another thing entirely. Are you enjoying MW4’s early access campaign? Let us know your thoughts on the Insider Gaming D i scord server . For more Insider Gaming coverage, check out the news that WARDOGS’ third season is being moved forward . Also, don’t forget to sign up for our weekly newsletter . Grant has been gaming for 30+ years and in the industry for 10+. You'll probably find him playing a post-apocalyptic game or an extraction shooter somewhere.

sources.title: When will Modern Warfare 4 be on Game Pass?
sources.text: COD: MW4 will be on Game Pass, but not at launch Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 (2026) will not be on Xbox Game Pass at launch, which may came as a point of frustration to those COD fans who were hoping that the company's involvement with Microsoft would mean a day-one Game Pass availability. However, that doesn't mean that it's not coming at some point in the future, as I'll lay out the details below. According to an official press release from the development team, Modern Warfare 4 is not going to be available on Xbox Game Pass until "Holiday 2027," roughly one year after its initial launch and release. Further details about exactly when in the year that will be are currently not available, but either way players can expect a long wait if they're dependant on Game Pass and don't want to purchase a copy for themselves. MW4 will still be available to buy on Xbox from its initial launch date of October 23, 2026, but not on the Game Pass subscription service. If you want an alternative until then, there are still a multitude of Call of Duty games currently available on Xbox Game Pass to download as part of the service, going all the way back to Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War from 2020. Alternatively, if you're less brand-loyal and just want to find an online military shooter to experience with friends, Battlefield 6 is also available for free on Game Pass. © GamesRadar+. sources.title: Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World details online content, offline Battle Arena, and Wrangler’s Gauntlet
sources.text: Publisher and developer Square Enix , and developer TOSE have released new information and screenshots for Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World introducing online content, the offline Battle Arena, and the new roguelike mode Wrangler’s Gauntlet. ■ Team Up With Wranglers the World Over and Take on Joint Battles Together! After you progress some way through the story of Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World , you’ll unlock a host of online content. These modes are enabled for cross-platform play, meaning you can enjoy them with anyone, regardless of their chosen gaming system. One of those modes is Online Joint Battles, where you can team up with other wranglers to test your skills against massive monsters together. There are daily quests to try your hand at, as well as special events featuring infamous monsters from across the Dragon Quest series, with fantastic rewards for those able to overcome the challenge! —With three difficulties of regular quests to choose from, you can select the level of challenge that best matches your current party’s strength. —Once you’ve chosen the quest you want to take on, you can start the matching process to find other players. You can also choose to play alone if you wish. —During battle, you can talk with your teammates using a selection of simple preset messages—and you’ll need to communicate if you want to emerge victorious! —When you use healing and support skills on allied parties in battle, you’ll boost your collective Team Bonus. This multiplier increases the damage that everyone can inflict on the enemy and boosts the effectiveness of healing abilities. —Keep an eye out for super-tough Special Quests that feature special monsters. These events regularly come and go, so be sure to give them a try if you’re feeling strong enough. You can earn monster eggs as rewards for completing Online Joint Battles and other challenges. The monsters that hatch forth can then be added to your party! —Eggs come in four colors, and all sorts of monsters can be inside. ■ Connect Online to Access a Wealth of Extra Content! In addition to Online Joint Battles, connecting online allows you to battle against other players in Ranked Matches to improve your global ranking, fight parties that players have uploaded via the Wranglers Society and much more. However, because the online content, such as Online Joint Battles and Ranked Matches, is intended to be a fair test of your monster wrangling skills, the Wrangler’s Spirit ability won’t activate in these game modes. —In Ranked Matches, you compete against other players of a similar ability to yours. There are seven main ranks, from Beginner to Legendary, and the goal is to rise as far you can in the standings. —Every victory rewards you with Ranking Points. Your total at the end of a season determines your rank. Perform well and you might earn promotion to a higher rank, with rewards for doing so! —In Private Matches, you can customize the rules of battle, such as setting the number of rounds or the times you can swap in your reserves. —Head over to the Online Hub, where other players are represented, to participate in the Wranglers Society. By speaking to the wranglers there, you can battle against their parties, so be sure to take your strongest monsters along with you. —Win a battle in the Wranglers Society and you’ll get to spin the roulette wheel to determine your reward, with items, mini medals and other great prizes up for grabs. —The Online Shop has some valuable items for sale. The lineup changes depending on the day of the week and your progress through the story, so check back regularly to see what new stock has come in. ■ The Battle Arena, Where Monster Wranglers Go to Test Their Mettle! In addition to the online content, there’s also a fully offline Battle Arena to enjoy, which Bianca and Nera will discover upon visiting Witherwood Castle. In these contests, you’ll send the monsters you’ve raised into battles that will determine the strongest wrangler in the kingdom. This Battle Arena features both regular battles and joint battles, each with seven difficulty categories from G up to A. With rewards on offer for completing a category, the Battle Arena is the perfect place to test your skills or take a break from adventuring. —In the regular Arena Battles, you have to win all three matches in a category to complete it. Your monsters’ HP and MP will be fully restored between matches, so you can always fight to the max. Once you pay the entry fee, it’s time to start battling! —During battle, you can choose the general tactics you want your monsters to follow. Keep close tabs on how each battle plays out and adjust your tactics accordingly. —In Joint Battles at the arena, you can set the tactics for your main party and your reserves, as well as for the other monster wranglers who fight alongside you. ■ An All-New Roguelike Mode for Extended Replayability! Progress even further through the story and a new challenge will unlock in the Battle Arena called the “Wrangler’s Gauntlet” that will truly test your ability as a monster wrangler! Devised by Scruffy, the Wrangler’s Gauntlet provides you with a selection of monsters that changes each time you attempt the challenge. You must use what you’re given to build a party capable of winning 50 consecutive battles. The monsters you befriend here, and the items you obtain, can’t be taken out on your adventures, but with different starting monsters each time and opponents that change with every new attempt, no two runs are ever the same. The roguelike elements offer a fresh perspective on monster wrangling! —The challenge begins once you receive your monsters from Scruffy. He’ll even tell you which monsters you’ll face off against in the next battle, meaning you can tailor your party to best deal with each different opponent. —After winning a battle, you’ll have the opportunity to strengthen your party. sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: Dementium II coming to Steam on October 20
sources.text: Atooi will release horror first-person shooter sequel Dementium II for PC via Steam on October 20, the developer announced. Dementium II first launched for DS on May 4, 2010, followed by PC on December 17, 2013. The Steam release is a new, “remastered” version. Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : The DS horror sequel, reborn. William Redmoor wakes with fresh staples in his skull, inside an institution for the criminally insane, where the walls keep peeling back to expose something worse. Fight, solve, and survive your way out. The cult classic, remastered. The last thing William Redmoor remembers is the Doctor’s scalpel. Now he wakes at the Bright Dawn Treatment Center with a new wound and an old accusation: the records say he murdered his wife. In his cell, a postcard is waiting. The handwriting is his own. It tells him to run. The staff insist he’s recovering. But since the surgery, reality has started to split, and the “hospital” keeps tearing open into a demented version of itself. The Doctor has a theory about why: whatever was wrong inside your head, we let it out! Escaping Bright Dawn is only the beginning. Outside lies an empty village and a countryside crawling with things that shouldn’t exist. Letters signed by his wife lead him deeper. She says she’s waiting for him. Faithful to the Original. Rebuilt for Today You don’t need to have played the first game to survive this one. Here’s what you need to know. In Dementium: The Ward , William Redmoor woke up in a hospital with no memory, surrounded by creatures that had no business being alive. Newspaper clippings claimed he had murdered his wife. Visions of his daughter led him deeper into the dark, while a man in black who called himself the Doctor watched every step. William fought his way down to the basement to face him. It didn’t end the way he hoped. Dementium II begins where that ending left him: under the Doctor’s knife.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Fortnite is coming to Linux so we may soon be able to play it and other games like Apex Legends on Steam Deck and Steam Machine
sources.text: Epic Games is officially working on bringing its battle royale shooter Fortnite to Linux. The announcement was tucked away at the bottom of Epic's widely mocked blog post revealing the new, "vibe-coded" Epic Games Store, which is also coming to Linux. At the time, Epic explained it's going to be working with Linux distro maintainers on a set of security requirements needed to run Fortnite. Distros - short for distributions - are operating system variants of Linux, each with its own goals and prioritised system operations. Valve's SteamOS, for instance, is based on Arch Linux. Because of the many discrepancies between Linux distros, each would need to implement Epic's security requirements individually if they want Fortnite to run on their operating system. Fortnite will arrive on Linux via the EGS launcher, but only if a "critical mass of distro maintainers" is reached. Epic didn't specify numbers. This is big news for several reasons. For one, the move would likely make Fortnite playable on SteamOS PCs and handhelds, including Steam Machine and Steam Deck. Furthermore, even if that "critical mass" is never reached, Epic says its work will be available to other developers interested in bringing their games to Linux. Perhaps the biggest reason this is a big deal, however, has to do with Easy Anti-Cheat, the Epic-owned anti-cheat service used in Fortnite and dozens of other games - including Dead by Daylight , Rocket League , Apex Legends , and even Elden Ring . While Easy Anti-Cheat does support Linux, including for some of the games just mentioned, many developers choose not to enable it , simply because its "Linux implementation couldn't offer the same level of protection as our Windows implementation," as Epic explained in a separate blog post . This is why many games that use Easy Anti-Cheat aren't playable on Steam Machine or Steam Deck . The post even names Valve specifically, saying the team will "continue its open line of communication" to support Steam hardware devices "to the maximum extent technically possible". Part of the reason Linux has been a difficult problem for anti-cheat makers to solve is the platform's open nature, meaning certain - required - system-level protections are not guaranteed. On Windows, you can ask users to enable features like TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot , which create that secure environment once hardware requirements are met. While some of that work can be done on Linux, it requires the interest and participation of distro maintainers. Easy Anti-Cheat plans to use Linux features such as signed kernel, signed kernel modules, and secure boot with attestation to achieve that goal. "These requirements build on work that distribution maintainers already do," explains Epic, "and the more distributions that meet these requirements by default, the fewer players will need to change their setup to play." The goal is to "bring the level of protection much closer to par with Windows". There is no timeline for any of this at present, but Easy Anti-Cheat will test the announced plans in Fortnite first before making them available to other developers. In other words, if Fortnite gets a release date on Linux, you'll know the work has paid off and we're closer than ever to achieving anti-cheat parity between Windows and Linux.

The odds might be stacked against you but with awesome powers, a winning personality and up to four-player local co-up on your side, the Smogulan Empire’s days are numbered! Take a deep breath and dive deep into an action-packed, pun-filled adventure that drags you kicking and screaming through the wonderful world of Troma. Enjoy cameos from gore-filled classics such as Class of Nuke ‘Em High, Poultrygeist: Night of the Chicken Dead, and Sgt. Kabukiman N.Y.P.D.—reimagined in the Saturday morning cartoon style that made this franchise so unforgettable! sources.title: Resident Evil Veronica: Everything you need to know about the Code Veronica remake
sources.text: Resident Evil Veronica is bringing 2000's Code Veronica into the modern era in 2027 Resident Evil Veronica is the official title for the long-rumored remake of Resident Evil: Code Veronica. Announced as part of a very memorable surprise reveal during the Summer Game Fest 2026 showcase , Resident Evil Veronica will bring back the cult classic 2000 release with a modern makeover. With Capcom confirming the upcoming horror game will be arriving in 2027 , the developer is setting out to "preserve the essence of the original game", but just like the many excellent Resi remakes we've seen over the years, you can expect shiny new and improved graphics, plenty of gameplay enhancements, and more. There's a lot of excitement surrounding the new game , with the remake quickly racking up two million Steam wishlists within a month of its reveal . That's not so surprising given Capcom's winning streak in 2026, with its new sci-fi IP Pragmata and Resident Evil Requiem , which has already earned its place (along with many other Resi games) as one of the best survival horror games around right now. So whether you can hardly wait to join Claire and Chris Redfield or you're curious to learn more about their sibling team-up, read on as I break down everything you need to know about Resident Evil Veronica. The Resident Evil Veronica release date is currently set for sometime in 2027 . The surprise announcement of Code Veronica's return came with the news of the 2027 launch window, but we're still awaiting an exact release date to be confirmed. The line-up of upcoming games dropping in early 2027 is already quite stacked, with the likes of Stranger Than Heaven, Fable, and Exodus, and more all releasing within the first four months of the year. I'm curious to see if Resident Evil Veronica will add another release to a very busy period, but it would be fitting if it was released later in 2027 for the spooky season. I'll be keeping an eye out for updates from Capcom. Capcom confirmed the Resident Evil Veronica platforms in the initial reveal trailer, with the remake set to land on PC, PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox Series X . Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week With lots of Resi goodness landing on the Switch 2 in 2026, it's great to see Veronica complete the set and join the likes of Resident Evil 2 Remake , Resident Evil 3 Remake , and Resident Evil 4 Remake along with Resident Evil 7, Resident Evil Village , and Requiem. Better still, it appears Veronica will be launching on all platforms simultaneously in 2027. I'm glad Resident Evil Veronica will have a "reimagined story" – remakes need reinvention to survive Resident Evil Veronica's story is set to be something of a reimagining of the original game's storyline that promises to deliver a "chilling new entry in survival horror". Claire Redfield, who appeared in Resident Evil 2 Remake alongside Leon Kennedy, is one of two leading protagonists, with Veronica taking place three months after the biological disaster she survived her way through in Raccoon City. As we see a nod to in the initial reveal trailer when the older woman says, "I hate to say, but your brother is, well, quite odd", Claire has traveled to France in search of her sibling, Chris Redfield. But things take a turn when Umbrella steps in (those dastardly fiends!). Umbrella captures Claire and brings her to the mysterious, remote Rockfort Island. And because she can't get a moment's peace, this island has also been hit by another biological disaster. With no cozy family reunion on the cards, Claire now finds herself in another fight for survival in classic Resi fashion. The original game became something of a cult classic for some of its goofier aspects and memorable moments, of which fans have been fondly remembering since the remake was officially confirmed . It also features Resident Evil 1 and 5 baddie Albert Wesker back in his evil villain throne for one of the most iconic instalments in the franchise. With a Wesker clone named Zeno having appeared in Resident Evil Requiem, I have a feeling Capcom is building out the connective tissue between Code Veronica, as the most popular among the Resident Evil spin-offs, and Resident Evil 5 – which could well be the next mainline Resi game to get the remake treatment. Either way, it's clear that Capcom is aiming to keep the essence of the Code Veronica alive, and I can't wait to see how they bring this story into the modern era and put a fresh spin on it. Resident Evil Veronica's gameplay will be modernized to bring it in line with some of the latest Resident Evil games in the series. While we've yet to see any gameplay in action, or see what changes it will include, we expect it to be like other remakes in the Resident Evil timeline , with all of the survival horror goodness that comes with. And while the reveal trailer was in first-person to keep us guessing, a producer has confirmed Veronica will be a third-person experience . In the original, which was broken up into chapters, there were more playable characters during certain sections. While Claire still took center stage for the most part, there was also Steve Burnside, a prisoner on Rockfort Island, and Chris Redfield, who we haven't seen since Resident Evil Village. We're guessing this will once again be the case in Resident Evil Veronica. For more Resi goodness, check out our ranking of the best Resident Evil games , or explore the Resident Evil movie .
